topic: Hax: A Minimalist Terminal-Native Coding Agent Written in C

key_points: Primary source: single native C binary, small dependency set, starts instantly, uses only a few MB of RAM so more is left for local LLMs
Local models are first-class: auto-discovers llama.cpp server model and runtime capabilities, no custom provider config needed
Terminal-respecting: streaming Markdown and live tool output reflowed for display, only redraws current line/input area, preserves native scrollback
Inspectable: Ctrl+T transcript view shows exactly what was sent to the model and its reply; optional wire protocol trace
Supports OpenAI (+compatible), Anthropic (+compatible), Codex (via ChatGPT subscription), OpenRouter, llama.cpp, ollama
Well-behaved Unix tool: XDG paths, clean stdout in -p one-shot mode, plain-text config/session files, composition via subprocesses instead of plugins
Deliberately omits MCP, plugins, permission prompts, IDE panels — philosophy.md documents each omission and the pattern that covers the need
MIT license, runs on Linux, macOS, FreeBSD, OpenBSD; Windows via WSL; Homebrew tap + AUR + prebuilt static binaries
Official homepage with asciinema-recorded demo session (gpt-5.6-luna at high reasoning effort, replayed at 2x)
Target audience: developers who live in the terminal, run local models, audit what their tools do, package for distros, or run agents where resources are scarce
Positioning: 'fancy new AI tech in an old-school minimalist package'
Quick start: interactive REPL, hax -p one-shot, hax -c continue, hax --resume
HN Show/launch story, 114 points, posted 2026-08-12
Positive reception: users report clean, fast performance with local models and llama.cpp on MacBook Pro
Author explains C choice: easiest way to achieve minimal resource footprint, and the language he knows well; demo recorded with asciinema
Discussion: models adapt well to hax tools instead of native codex tools; GPT models work fine
Debate over why start a new project in C today — portability and minimalism defended by commenters
Not to be confused with Haxe (haxe.org)
Direct C-language competitor: 'AI coding agent in C. Single binary, zero runtime deps, every major LLM provider'
26 stars — much smaller community than hax (225 stars)
Confirms the niche of C-based minimalist coding agents is emerging but still tiny
Rust-based terminal coding agent (804 stars) — the main non-C alternative in the same minimalist-terminal space
LLM-native code understanding, OS-native sandboxing, multi-provider support
Shows the contrast: Rust vs C for terminal-native agents; hax is the C representative

angles: The 'minimalist C binary' angle: why a few-MB native C binary is a deliberate counterpoint to resource-hungry JS/Python agents, and what it means for local-LLM workflows
Local-first philosophy: hax treats llama.cpp local models as first-class, auto-discovering the model — a differentiator for privacy/offline users
The anti-feature manifesto: hax deliberately omits MCP, plugins, and permission prompts, and documents why — a contrarian take on the modern agent feature race
Terminal-respect as UX: streaming Markdown and live tool output that preserves native scrollback, unlike agents that take over the terminal
C vs Rust vs JS for coding agents: hax (C) vs VT Code (Rust) vs mainstream JS/Python agents — a portability and resource-footprint comparison
Inspectability and trust: Ctrl+T transcript view and wire-protocol tracing for users who audit what their AI tools do
The HN reception: 114 points and the debate over starting new projects in C in 2026
